examples.en: I can hear the sound of horse hooves from far away.

examples.ko: 소는 발굽이 두 갈래로 갈라져 있어요.
examples.en: A cow's hoof is split into two parts.

examples.ko: 대장장이가 말 발굽에 편자를 박아 줬어요.
examples.en: The blacksmith nailed a horseshoe onto the horse's hoof.

examples.ko: 농장에서는 소 발굽을 정기적으로 다듬어 줘요.
examples.en: On farms, they trim the cows' hooves regularly.
The deer kicked the ground with its hooves and ran away.

examples.ko: 눈 위에 사슴 발굽 자국이 길게 나 있어요.
examples.en: There are long deer hoof prints in the snow.

explain: '발'은 사람과 동물에게 다 쓰지만 '발굽'은 말, 소, 사슴처럼 굽이 있는 동물의 발끝 단단한 부분에만 써요. 돼지 발로 만든 요리는 '발굽'이 아니라 '족발'이라고 불러요.
explain_en: '발' (foot) is used for both people and animals, but '발굽' is only the hard tip of the foot of hoofed animals such as horses, cows and deer. A dish made from pig feet is called '족발', not '발굽'.

examples.en: The child's cheeks are flushed, maybe because he was embarrassed.

examples.ko: 추운 날 밖에 있었더니 코끝이 발그레해졌어요.
examples.en: After being outside on a cold day, the tip of my nose turned rosy.
Her face was flushed, so I worried she might have a fever.
Those rosy cheeks like apples are so cute.

examples.ko: 칭찬을 듣자 그녀의 뺨이 발그레하게 달아올랐어요.
examples.en: When she heard the compliment, her cheeks flushed pink.

examples.ko: 아침에 본 아이의 얼굴이 아직도 발그레했어요.
examples.en: The child's face I saw in the morning was still flushed.

explain: '빨갛다'보다 연하고 은은하게 붉은 느낌이에요. 주로 볼, 얼굴, 코끝처럼 부끄러움이나 추위로 살짝 붉어진 모습에 써요.
explain_en: It describes a softer, gentler red than '빨갛다'. It is mostly used for cheeks, faces or the tip of the nose turning slightly red from shyness or cold.

examples.ko: 화가 나서 편지를 발기발기 찢어 버렸어요.
examples.en: I was so angry that I tore the letter to shreds.
My puppy chewed my socks to shreds.
I tore the paper into pieces and put it in the trash can.
The cat tore the sofa to shreds.

examples.ko: 어린 동생이 책 한 권을 발기발기 찢어 놓았어요.
examples.en: My little sibling tore a whole book to shreds.
The plastic bag was torn to shreds by the wind.

explain: 종이나 천 같은 것을 마구 잘게 찢는 모습에 써요. '갈기갈기'도 같은 뜻으로 많이 말하고, 보통 '찢다', '찢어지다'와 함께 나와요.
explain_en: It describes tearing paper or cloth roughly into small pieces, and usually goes with '찢다' or '찢어지다'. '갈기갈기' is another common word with the same meaning.

examples.ko: 그는 이 회사의 발기인 중 한 명이에요.
examples.en: He is one of the promoters who set up this company.

examples.ko: 동호회를 만든 발기인들이 모여서 회의를 했어요.
examples.en: The people who started the club got together for a meeting.

examples.ko: 발기인으로 이름을 올리려면 어떻게 해야 해요?
examples.en: What do I have to do to put my name down as a founding member?
At the founders' meeting, we decided on the name of the group.
I looked into how many founding members are needed.

examples.ko: 발기인에게 먼저 연락해 보는 게 어때요?
examples.en: Why don't you try contacting the founder first?

explain: 모임이나 회사, 단체를 만들자고 처음 제안하고 준비에 나선 사람이에요. 이미 만든 사람을 가리키는 '창립자'와 달리 설립을 제안하고 준비하는 단계의 사람을 말해요.
explain_en: This is a person who first proposes and prepares the founding of a club, company or organization. Unlike '창립자' (founder), it points to someone at the proposing and preparing stage.

examples.en: That player's footwork is really fast.
Footwork is important when you dance.

examples.ko: 권투 선수는 발놀림 하나로 상대를 피했어요.
examples.en: The boxer dodged his opponent with footwork alone.
My footwork is clumsy, so my steps keep getting tangled.

examples.ko: 축구 감독이 어린 선수의 발놀림을 칭찬했어요.
examples.en: The soccer coach praised the young player's footwork.

examples.ko: 가벼운 발놀림에 맞춰 음악이 점점 빨라졌어요.
examples.en: The music got faster to match the light footwork.

explain: 스포츠나 춤에서 발을 움직이는 솜씨를 말할 때 써요. '손놀림', '몸놀림'처럼 몸의 부분 뒤에 '-놀림'을 붙인 짝말이 있고, 같은 뜻으로 '풋워크'라고도 해요.
explain_en: It is used for how skillfully someone moves their feet in sports or dance. It has sibling words like '손놀림' and '몸놀림', and people also say '풋워크' for the same thing.

examples.en: The volunteer group's kick-off ceremony is tomorrow morning.
Please be sure to attend the cheer squad's launching ceremony.
We started our activities right after the kick-off ceremony.

examples.ko: 시장님이 청년 서포터즈 발대식에서 축사를 했어요.
examples.en: The mayor gave a congratulatory speech at the youth supporters' launching ceremony.

examples.ko: 발대식 준비 때문에 어제 늦게까지 일했어요.
examples.en: I worked late yesterday preparing for the kick-off ceremony.

examples.ko: 올해 발대식은 비 때문에 실내에서 했어요.
examples.en: This year's kick-off ceremony was held indoors because of the rain.

explain: 서포터즈, 봉사단, 대표팀 같은 모임이 공식 활동을 시작하며 여는 행사예요. '출범식'과 비슷하게 쓰이고, 입학식이나 졸업식처럼 '-식'이 붙지만 '시작'을 알리는 행사예요.
explain_en: It is the event a group such as supporters, a volunteer corps or a team holds to officially begin its activities. It is used much like '출범식', and marks a start rather than an entrance or graduation.

examples.en: I sprang up the moment the alarm rang.

examples.ko: 소파에 누워 있던 아버지가 발딱 일어나 문을 열었어요.
examples.en: My father, who was lying on the sofa, jumped up and opened the door.
Startled, I sat bolt upright in bed.

examples.ko: 내가 이름을 부르자 아이가 발딱 일어나 달려왔어요.
examples.en: When I called his name, the child hopped up and ran over.

examples.ko: 쓰러졌던 선수가 발딱 일어나서 다시 뛰었어요.
examples.en: The player who had fallen popped back up and ran again.
I woke with a start from dozing and got off the bus.

explain: 누워 있거나 앉아 있다가 갑자기 몸을 일으키는 모습에 주로 써요. '벌떡'보다 작고 가볍게 일어나는 느낌이고, 보통 '일어나다'와 함께 나와요.
explain_en: It mostly describes suddenly getting up from lying or sitting, and usually goes with '일어나다'. It feels a bit smaller and lighter than '벌떡'.

examples.en: The puppy flopped onto its back and showed its belly.
The cat rolled onto its back in the sunshine.
The child slipped and fell flat on his back.
I was tired, so I just flopped down onto the bed.
When I lay flat on the floor, my body relaxed.

examples.ko: 거북이가 뒤집혀 발라당 누운 채 버둥거렸어요.
examples.en: The turtle was flipped over on its back, struggling.

explain: 가볍게 뒤로 눕거나 넘어지는 모습이고, 강아지, 고양이, 아기처럼 귀여운 대상에 잘 어울려요. 더 크고 둔한 느낌은 '벌러덩'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It describes lightly flopping or falling onto one's back, and suits cute subjects like puppies, cats and babies. The bigger, heavier version is '벌러덩'.

examples.ko: 이 질병의 발병률은 해마다 높아지고 있어요.
examples.en: The incidence rate of this disease is rising every year.
Exercising lowers the incidence of heart disease.
The incidence rate differs a lot from region to region.

examples.ko: 연구팀은 백신 접종 후 발병률을 조사했어요.
examples.en: The research team studied the incidence rate after vaccination.
The incidence of flu goes up a lot in winter.

examples.ko: 이 병은 어른에 비해 아이의 발병률도 낮지 않아요.
examples.en: This disease also has a considerable incidence among children compared with adults.

explain: 뉴스나 논문에서 많이 나오는 말이에요. 새로 병에 걸린 사람의 비율은 '발병률', 이미 병을 앓고 있는 사람의 비율은 '유병률'이라고 해서 구별해요.
explain_en: This word appears often in news and papers. The share of people newly falling ill is '발병률', while the share of people currently living with the illness is '유병률'.

examples.en: The government said it would root out voice phishing crimes.
Citizens demanded that corruption be eradicated at its roots.

examples.ko: 문제의 원인을 발본색원하지 않으면 또 생길 거예요.
examples.en: If we don't root out the cause of the problem, it will happen again.
We will stamp out the irregularities this time.

examples.ko: 경찰이 가짜 약 판매 조직을 발본색원했어요.
examples.en: The police wiped out the fake medicine sales ring.

examples.ko: 말로만 말고 문제를 발본색원하는 방법을 찾아야 해요.
examples.en: We need to find a way to actually root out the problem, not just talk.

explain: 나쁜 일이나 비리, 악습을 뿌리부터 완전히 없앨 때 쓰는 한자어예요. 주로 뉴스나 연설에서 나오고, 일상 대화에서는 '뿌리를 뽑다'라고 말해요.
explain_en: This Sino-Korean word is used when completely getting rid of wrongdoing, corruption or bad habits down to the root. It mostly appears in news and speeches, and in daily talk people say '뿌리를 뽑다'.

en: make an excuse; make a pretext; evade

examples.ko: 이제 와서 발뺌하면 안 되죠. 처음에는 분명히 동의했잖아요.
examples.en: You can't deny it now. You clearly agreed at first.

examples.ko: 발뺌만 하는 사람과는 같이 일하기 힘들어요.
examples.en: It's hard to work with someone who only dodges responsibility.

examples.ko: 그는 자기가 한 일을 끝까지 발뺌했어요.
examples.en: He denied what he did to the very end.
Even though the evidence came out, he keeps denying it.
He didn't want to take responsibility, so he tried to wriggle out of it.
Don't try to dodge it. Please tell me honestly.

explain: 자기가 한 일이나 책임을 '나는 아니다'라며 피하려는 것이에요. 이유를 대는 '변명하다'와 달리 책임을 빠져나가려는 부정적인 느낌이 강하고, '시치미를 떼다'와도 비슷하게 쓰여요.
explain_en: It means trying to escape blame or responsibility by saying 'it wasn't me'. Unlike '변명하다' (to give reasons), it has a strong negative feel of slipping out of responsibility, and is close to '시치미를 떼다'.

examples.en: Greece is the birthplace of the Olympics.

examples.ko: 이 학교 자리가 근대 교육의 발상지래요.
examples.en: I heard this school site is the cradle of modern education.
That place is famous as the birthplace of jazz.

examples.ko: 이곳이 그 운동의 발상지라는 표지판이 있어요.
examples.en: There is a sign saying this is where the movement began.
I went to see the monument built at the birthplace.

examples.ko: 문화의 발상지를 따라 걷는 여행 코스가 인기예요.
examples.en: A trip route that follows the cradles of culture is popular.

explain: 문화, 운동, 사상, 제도가 처음 시작된 곳을 말해요. 강이 시작되는 곳은 '발원지'라고 하니까 구별해서 써요.
explain_en: It refers to the place where a culture, movement, idea or system first began. The place where a river begins is called '발원지', so keep the two apart.

examples.ko: 계약 조건은 발표 전까지 절대 발설하지 마세요.
examples.en: Please never disclose the contract terms before the announcement.

examples.ko: 친구가 제 비밀을 멋대로 발설해서 화가 났어요.
examples.en: I was angry because my friend revealed my secret without permission.

examples.ko: 이 이야기는 아직 발설할 수 없어요.
examples.en: I can't disclose this story yet.
They are investigating who leaked the information.

examples.ko: 합격자 명단은 공식 발표 전에 발설하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You must not reveal the list of successful applicants before the official announcement.
We still don't know who divulged it.

explain: '말하다'보다 무거운 말로, 비밀이나 기밀, 내부 정보를 입 밖에 낼 때 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '말하다'나 '비밀을 흘리다'처럼 더 쉬운 말을 많이 써요.
explain_en: It is a heavier word than '말하다' and is used when letting out a secret, confidential matter or inside information. In daily talk people use easier phrases like '말하다' or '비밀을 흘리다'.

examples.en: I don't know who the sender of this email is.
The sender's address is written incorrectly.
The sender's name on the parcel is printed faintly.
I contacted the sender and asked them to take it back.
The sender gets a notification when the parcel arrives.

examples.ko: 발송자와 수신자 정보를 모두 적어 주세요.
examples.en: Please write down both the sender and recipient information.

explain: 우편, 택배, 이메일처럼 무언가를 보내는 사람이에요. 반대말은 '수신자'이고, 일상에서는 '보내는 사람'이라고 많이 해요. 전화나 문자를 건 쪽은 보통 '발신자'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is the person who sends something such as mail, a parcel or an email. The opposite is '수신자', and in daily life people often say '보내는 사람'. The party who makes a call or sends a text is usually called '발신자'.

examples.ko: 아이가 사 달라고 바닥에서 발악하듯 울었어요.
examples.en: The child cried on the floor as if throwing a wild fit to get it bought.
He struggled desperately to win until the very end.

examples.ko: 마지막 순간까지 살려고 발악하는 모습이 안타까웠어요.
examples.en: It was sad to see it fighting desperately to live until the last moment.
There's no use in raging and struggling now.

examples.ko: 동생이 숙제를 하기 싫다고 발악하고 있어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling is throwing a fit because he doesn't want to do his homework.
Don't thrash around like that now.

explain: 막다른 곳에 몰려 악을 쓰고 몸부림치는 모습이에요. '노력하다'와 달리 보기 좋지 않다는 부정적인 느낌이 있고, '마지막 발악'이라는 말을 자주 해요.
explain_en: It describes shouting and thrashing about when one is cornered. Unlike '노력하다' (to make an effort), it has a negative feel of looking unseemly, and '마지막 발악' (a last desperate struggle) is a common phrase.

examples.ko: 체육 시간에 반 친구들과 발야구를 했어요.
examples.en: We played kickball with my classmates in PE.
Lots of kids are playing kickball on the field.

examples.ko: 발야구는 규칙이 쉬워서 누구나 할 수 있어요.
examples.en: Kickball has easy rules, so anyone can play.
The kickball match was cancelled because of the rain.
In kickball, I always play the outfield.

examples.ko: 주말에 이웃 가족과 발야구 대회에 나갈 거예요.
examples.en: This weekend we're going to enter a kickball tournament with our neighbors.

explain: 학교 체육 시간이나 가족 모임에서 많이 하는 놀이 같은 경기예요. 외래어로 '킥볼'이라고도 해요.
explain_en: It is a game often played in school PE classes or at family gatherings. It is also called '킥볼', a loanword.

examples.en: The source of the Han River is in Taebaek, Gangwon Province.

examples.ko: 이 강의 발원지를 찾아 산을 올랐어요.
examples.en: I climbed the mountain to find the source of this river.
The closer to the source, the clearer the water.
They say there is a small spring at the source.
The source of the Nakdong River is also in Taebaek.

examples.ko: 이 병의 발원지가 어디인지 아직 밝혀지지 않았어요.
examples.en: Where this disease originated has not been found out yet.

explain: 강이 처음 시작되는 곳을 말해요. 병이나 유행이 시작된 곳에 비유해서 쓰기도 해요. 문화나 운동이 시작된 곳은 보통 '발상지'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is the place where a river begins. It is also used figuratively for where a disease or trend started. The place where a culture or movement began is usually called '발상지'.

examples.en: The funeral procession leaves at eight tomorrow morning.
I'll let you know when the date of the funeral departure is set.

examples.ko: 발인 전에 가족들이 마지막으로 인사를 드렸어요.
examples.en: Before the procession left, the family said their final goodbyes.
I took a day off to attend the funeral procession.

examples.ko: 할머니 발인이 오전 열 시에 있어요.
examples.en: Grandmother's funeral procession is at ten in the morning.

examples.ko: 발인까지 마치고 나서야 조금 쉴 수 있었어요.
examples.en: I could only rest a little after the procession was over.

explain: 장례에서 시신을 모시고 장지로 떠나는 절차예요. 보통 3일장의 마지막 날 아침이고, 부고에 '발인 ○월 ○일'처럼 적혀 있어요.
explain_en: This is the step in a funeral where the deceased is taken from the funeral hall toward the burial place. It is usually on the last morning of a three-day funeral, and obituary notices list it like '발인 ○월 ○일'.

examples.en: The client asked for a design change.
I checked the contract again with the client who ordered the construction.
The schedule changed according to the client's request.
I sent the quotation to the client.
The client for this building is the city hall.

examples.ko: 발주자 승인이 나야 다음 단계로 넘어가요.
examples.en: We can move on to the next stage only after the client approves.

explain: 공사, 물품, 용역 같은 일을 맡기는 쪽을 말해요. 일을 받아서 하는 쪽은 '수주자'나 '시공사'라고 하고, 현장에서는 '갑'이라고도 해요.
explain_en: It refers to the side that commissions work such as construction, goods or services. The side that takes on the work is called '수주자' or '시공사', and on site people also say '갑'.

examples.ko: 어린아이가 어른한테 그렇게 말하다니 참 발칙해요.
examples.en: It's quite impertinent for a young child to talk to an adult like that.
It may sound cheeky, but I think differently.
Where did you learn such a cheeky thing to say?

examples.ko: 그 광고는 발칙한 상상력으로 화제가 됐어요.
examples.en: That ad became a hot topic for its audacious imagination.

examples.ko: 선생님께 거짓말을 하다니 발칙하기 짝이 없네요.
examples.en: Lying to your teacher is outrageously impertinent.

examples.ko: 발칙했지만 그 아이의 솔직함이 밉지 않았어요.
examples.en: It was cheeky, but I didn't dislike the child's frankness.

explain: 버릇없고 건방지다는 뜻이라 보통 어른이 아랫사람의 행동을 나무랄 때 써요. 요즘은 '발칙한 상상'처럼 재치 있고 튀는 것을 가볍게 칭찬하는 말로도 많이 써요.
explain_en: It means rude and presumptuous, so adults usually use it to scold the behavior of someone younger. Nowadays it is also often used lightly as praise for witty, daring things, as in '발칙한 상상'.
